summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She had recently stopped alcohol and was taking oxycodone intermittently. Initial labs showed elevated lactate due to dehydration, which improved with IV fluids. Imaging revealed no new liver lesions or acute abdominal pathology, with findings unchanged from prior scans. Stool and blood cultures showed no infection. Symptoms were attributed to polysubstance withdrawal, including alcohol and narcotics. She was weaned off oxycodone, restarted on liver medications, and started on hyoscyamine for abdominal cramping. Her condition improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up arranged and counseling recommended for alcohol use.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
